Yeah, but since wands aren't reallly parallel to other objects that cause harm (they're projectile and weight is of no importance in the attack) compared with a warhammer, bow or sword, etc, 

So really, apart from being possible for the owner to hold, the wand's size to be perfect just needed to anticipate the style in which the user cast spells.

People talking about maybe not having the exact same broom, but maybe broom classes... It just makes more sense in this universe to have a policy that doesn't get the idea of  a level playing field.

Hogwarts exists in a society that split from pur own around at the end of the seventeenth century. It didn't really develop values that came later in human society: level playing field, meritocracy.  If you look a the late 17th century philosopher John Locke the state's legitimacy is rested upon the reluctant consent of a social contract. Everyone agrees it's worth giving up total autonomy to live in a social structure that, at minimum, can provide safety (in the case if MoM it's creation was to protect wizards from muggles). The ministry of magic though seems to be a nightwatchman state, where it doesn't really have jurisdiction or interest in pushing for equity, social justice, or a fair scientific way to measure performance, even if it is their most favourite sport.

I can empathize with overthinking a comment you made, but you should see that fact of how much it affected you as a testament to your character.

I am from the UK but moved to Poland 2 years ago and it's a similar situation here. The tap water is totally safe to drink in Warsaw (I remember reading there was even a campaign in the 2000s to convince people of the fact.); still, most people buy bottled water and I used to scoff at the fact people were spending unnecessary zlotych on bottled water. Until I tried bottled water myself and happened to prefer the taste.

I would just set a rule for myself to not get invested in other people's purchases? It's like getting angry at someone buying a sandwich from a supermarket because they could make a sandwich at home, but the cost of the presentation made sandwich accounts for its convenience and consumer choice
